class.name: BehaviorTreePlayer
class.brief_description: Runs a behaviour tree for a character.
class.description: Add it as a child of the character and set [member behavior_tree]. It ticks the tree every physics tick (see [member update_mode]), and starts it again whenever it finishes, so it keeps deciding what the character does. The game shares values with the tree through [member blackboard]: [codeblock] func _on_vision_spotted(body): $BehaviorTreePlayer.blackboard["target"] = body [/codeblock]

method.name: get_last_status
method.description: What the tree returned on its last tick.

method.name: get_running_tree
method.description: The running copy of the tree's root task, to look at its tasks' state.

method.name: restart
method.description: Stops the tree, telling running tasks they're leaving, and starts it again from the beginning.

method.name: update
method.description: Ticks the tree once with [param delta] and returns its status. Call it yourself with [constant UPDATE_MANUAL].

members.member: Whether the tree runs. Turning it off stops the running tasks.
The node the tree controls. Its parent by default.

The values the tree's tasks share. When the tree starts, the tree's own values that this doesn't have are added to it, and the tasks then use this same dictionary, so the game can read and write it as they run. Setting a new dictionary restarts the tree.
When the tree ticks: see [enum UpdateMode].

signal.name: finished
signal.description: Emitted each time the tree finishes, with [constant BehaviorTask.SUCCESS] or [constant BehaviorTask.FAILURE]. It starts again on the next tick.

constants.constant: Every physics tick, the default, as most tasks move bodies.
Only when the game calls [method update].
